source: calc/cgglyph.py photos, bm_core_videos/9 and /10, decoded by tools/glyphdecode.py (tiles snapped to their own grey boxes, per-tile sub-block alignment, block-area means). Where the two batches' decodes differ, the one that better overlaps the black pixels of both photos. Advances from cgglyph's tables (bm_core_videos/10). Large glyphs whose tile snapped a block left (a full-height line in column 0) use the other batch, or are moved left one column. Large k moved two columns right, to where its photo shows it relative to the tile's grey box. Medium o rebuilt by hand (8 px wide, 2 px strokes, rows as decoded): its only photographed tile read too faintly at the sides. Medium G uses batch 9's full version (batch 10's lost its left column). Large rows corrected to the font's own lines (capitals and digits 1-19): 3 4 @ B E F G R Q up one, V and < adjusted; ) and [ are mirrors of ( and ] at rows 1-22; { } moved up with their bottom tip restored; " up one (matching '); | rows 1-21 from the cgfont.py photo. Medium ? and large &'(123<?EFKLMNPVWYZ[ read from both photos on a grid anchored to each tile's grey advance box (box width = advance - 1 px): medium ? was a column too narrow, the large ones a column too far right. Large C D G O Q S U X moved one column left, to where the grey-box readings of both photos place them.
note: rows[j][i] is the pixel at (x+left+i, y+top+j) for draw_string(x, y, ...); adv in px
shell_note: shell: the Python shell's font (10x18 cells, full cell stored, offsets 0,0), read from photos of the shell (bm_core_videos 6/165253, 6/165256, 7/221811, 11/173555 = calc/cgshell.py, every character): each occurrence binarised, aligned to the others within 1 px and voted. Cleaned by hand where one blurred cell drifted 1 px: # W X Y Z ^ _ y (and \ } as mirrors of / {); R [ ] | x kept from the earlier photos.
